title: Rarity Filter on the loot module header filters nothing
body:
## Summary
The header "Rarity Filter" buttons change state that only recolours the filter panel; no tab reads it.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/index.tsx:38 holds rarityFilter; it feeds only activeRarityColor (index.tsx:50) and LootFilters (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/LootFilters.tsx:149). LootTabPanels (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/LootTabPanels.tsx:243) takes no rarity prop, so the loot-table editor, treemap, simulators and EV panels ignore it. A control that changes nothing is a false affordance. Fixed means one of two product choices: wire the filter into the panels that list items (editor, treemap, world items), or remove it. That choice is the escalation.

## Flow
- Open Loot > any tab
- Click "Legendary" in Rarity Filter
- Only the filter panel recolours; every list and chart below is unchanged

## Expected impact
Designers stop trusting a filter that does nothing; removing or wiring it restores a truthful header. Wiring could break panels that assume the full roster.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the header control either works or is gone
Before: rarityFilter has 0 readers outside index.tsx/LootFilters.tsx (grep over src/: only a test passes "All")
After: wire: >=3 panels filter by rarity; remove: 0 dead controls
Method: probe
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence: grep -rn rarityFilter src -> sub_loot/index.tsx:38,50-53,88-90; LootFilters.tsx:124-153; src/__tests__/components/core-engine/loot-binding-tuner-panel.test.tsx:61 (passes "All"). LootTabPanels props (LootTabPanels.tsx:243-252) carry no rarity.
impact: Designers stop trusting a filter that does nothing; removing or wiring it restores a truthful header. Wiring could break panels that assume the full roster.

title: LOOT_ENTRY_METADATA is unconsumed and files 34 of 65 loot entries as Misc
body:
## Summary
The loot entity-metadata export has no importer, and its name regexes miss spears, maces, hammers, armour pieces, elixirs and accessories.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/data.ts:348 builds LOOT_ENTRY_METADATA from lootCategory/lootSubcategory (data.ts:322-346). git grep finds no code importer (only .harness-ui logs). Its regexes classify Bone Club, Hunting Spear, Wrath Hammer, Void Scythe, Copper Mace, Flame Whip (weapons), Chain Mail, Plate Greaves, Celestial Vestments (armour), Elixir/Antidote/Bomb/Grenade (consumables) and Signet/Pendant/Bracelet/Crown/Talisman (accessories) as Misc. Either wire it to the entity-metadata consumer it was built for (with correct classification) or delete it; the harness built it deliberately, so the choice is the operator's.

## Flow
- Run lootCategory over EXPANDED_ENTRIES
- 34 of 65 entries return Misc, ~20 of them obviously typed by name

## Expected impact
Removing ~45 dead lines, or making the metadata correct before anything reads it. Nothing visible breaks today because nothing reads it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no dead, wrong metadata in the loot data module
Before: 0 importers; 34/65 entries Misc (node probe of the shipped regexes)
After: delete: 0 dead lines; wire: Misc limited to materials/currency (~14)
Method: probe
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence: git grep LOOT_ENTRY_METADATA -- . -> only .harness-ui/guide.json, progress.json, harness.log. Probe: 65 entries, 34 Misc: Bone Club, Hunting Spear, Wrath Hammer, Void Scythe, Copper Mace, Flame Whip, Chain Mail, Plate Greaves, Celestial Vestments, Elixir of Fortitude, Mana Crystal, Antidote Vial, Divine Ambrosia, Fire Bomb, Smoke Grenade, Signet of the Wilds, Bone Talisman, Emerald Pendant, Crown of Whispers, Ward Bracelet, ...
impact: Removing ~45 dead lines, or making the metadata correct before anything reads it. Nothing visible breaks today because nothing reads it.

title: Unknown imported rarity flows into generated C++ as a non-existent enum value
body:
## Summary
resolveRarityName returns an unrecognised rarity string verbatim, and the C++ re-export prints it as EARPGItemRarity::<value>.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/codegen.ts:28 falls back to the stripped raw string when the rarity is not in RARITY_ENUM_VALUES; generateUE5LootTableCpp (codegen.ts:127-128 of the emitted body) then writes `E.MinRarity = EARPGItemRarity::Mythic;` as live code, which does not compile against EARPGItemRarity. Fixed: an unknown rarity is either flagged on import (an import warning naming the rows) or mapped to Common with a visible note, and the codegen never emits a value outside the enum.

## Flow
- Import { Entries: [{ Item: "X", MinRarity: "EARPGItemRarity::Mythic" }] }
- Open Re-export > C++
- Generated block contains EARPGItemRarity::Mythic, a compile error in UE

## Expected impact
Pasted C++ compiles; the designer learns at import time, not at UE build time. Mapping silently could hide data the designer meant.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - generated C++ only names real enum values
Before: 1 invalid enum literal per unknown-rarity row (walked case)
After: 0 invalid literals; >=1 visible import warning
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Pasted C++ compiles; the designer learns at import time, not at UE build time. Mapping silently could hide data the designer meant.
instrument: test: parseUE5LootTable + generateUE5LootTableCpp over a Mythic row; assert every EARPGItemRarity::X in output is in RARITY_ENUM_VALUES and the import reports the row

title: Loot editor weight slider clamps imported DropWeight above 100 and rounds fractions
body:
## Summary
The per-entry range input is fixed at 0-100 step 1, so an imported weight of 250 or 2.5 is silently rewritten on the first touch.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix/LootTableEntryList.tsx:36-41 renders `<input type="range" min={0} max={100}>` for every entry. parseUE5LootTable accepts any finite non-negative DropWeight (codegen.ts:64), so UE tables with weights like 250 or 0.5 import fine, display a thumb pinned at 100 and, on any drag or arrow key, are rewritten to an integer <=100, changing every row's share and the re-export. Fixed: the slider range follows the table (e.g. max = max(100, largest weight)) and step follows the data, or a numeric field accompanies it.

## Flow
- Import a table with DropWeight 250 on one row
- Press Right Arrow on that row's slider
- Weight becomes 100; share and re-export change

## Expected impact
Round-trip fidelity for real UE tables. A dynamic max changes slider sensitivity for the other rows.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - import -> edit -> re-export preserves weight scale
Before: weight 250 -> 100 after one key press (walked)
After: weight 250 -> 251 / preserved
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Round-trip fidelity for real UE tables. A dynamic max changes slider sensitivity for the other rows.
instrument: component test: render LootTableEntryList with weight 250, assert slider max >= 250 and a change event keeps scale

title: Loot editor undo merges two separate drags on the same slider into one step
body:
## Summary
The drag-coalescing ref is only reset by add/remove/undo, never at drag end, so a later drag on the same row overwrites the previous undo snapshot.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix/LootTableEditor.tsx:122-129 coalesces when lastWeightEditIdRef equals the edited id. Nothing resets it on pointerup/blur (LootTableEntryList.tsx:41 has only onChange). Drag row X 40->60, release, think, drag X 60->80: the second drag replaces the first snapshot, and one Undo returns to 40, losing the 60 state. Fixed: an onPointerUp/onKeyUp/onBlur commit boundary that clears the ref.

## Flow
- Drag a row weight 40 -> 60, release
- Later drag the same row 60 -> 80
- Click Undo once: weight returns to 40, not 60

## Expected impact
Undo matches what the designer did. Risk: too-eager boundary splits a single drag into many steps.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one undo per gesture
Before: 2 gestures -> 1 undo step (walked)
After: 2 gestures -> 2 undo steps
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Undo matches what the designer did. Risk: too-eager boundary splits a single drag into many steps.
instrument: component test on LootTableEditor: two change sequences separated by pointerUp, one Undo, assert the middle value

title: Loot row "share" ignores NothingWeight while the preview bar includes it
body:
## Summary
Two drop-probability calculations in one editor disagree once a table has a NothingWeight.

## Description
The per-row share divides by editorTotalWeight only (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix/LootTableEntryList.tsx:56) while the live preview bar divides by editorTotalWeight + nothingWeight (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix/LootTableEditor.tsx:66-70). Import a table with NothingWeight 50 over 50 item weight: a 10-weight row reads "20.0% share" while its bar segment and tooltip say 10.0%. Fixed: one helper, and either label the row share as "of item drops" or include NothingWeight.

## Flow
- Import { Entries: [...total 50], NothingWeight: 50 }
- Row shows 20.0% share; bar tooltip shows 10.0%

## Expected impact
One truth for drop odds on screen. Changing the row figure changes a number designers may be reading.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the editor states one drop probability per row
Before: 2 formulas, 2x disagreement at NothingWeight = item weight (walked)
After: 1 formula or an explicit conditional label
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: One truth for drop odds on screen. Changing the row figure changes a number designers may be reading.
instrument: component test rendering LootTableEditor after an import with NothingWeight; assert row share equals bar tooltip (or label says "of item drops")

title: Loot editor ships two JSON exports, one silently lossy
body:
## Summary
"Export JSON" prints name/weight/rarity/source only, while "Re-export" emits the UE5 shape with quantities and rarity range.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix/LootTableEditor.tsx:237 serialises 4 of 9 entry fields; generateUE5LootTableJson (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/codegen.ts:81) serialises the round-trip shape. A designer who copies "Export JSON" loses MinQuantity/MaxQuantity/MinRarity/MaxRarity and NothingWeight with no warning. Fixed: remove the debug export, or relabel it ("Preview (summary)") so only the UE5 shape is called an export. Product choice, so C.

## Flow
- Import a UE5 table with quantities
- Click Export JSON
- Quantities and NothingWeight are absent

## Expected impact
No second, lossy export path. Removing it removes a quick-look some may use.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one export, lossless
Before: 2 exports; the toolbar one carries 4/9 fields and no NothingWeight
After: 1 export (or 1 clearly labelled summary)
Method: probe
Result: better
Gate: direction
impact: No second, lossy export path. Removing it removes a quick-look some may use.

title: Affix roll simulator has two definitions of a godroll
body:
## Summary
The printed Godroll % is "all three slots land the single rarest affix", but the win cue fires on any tier-3 affix in any slot.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix/AffixRollSimulator/useAffixRollSimulator.tsx:67-73 computes (minWeight/total)^3 (rarest affix x3: (2/421)^3, ~1.1e-5 %, printed as 0.00%), while :108 and :135 flag a slot as a win when picks[i].tier === 3 (9 of 35 affixes, 33/421 = 7.8% of weight per slot, ~22% of spins show a cue). The header promises a ~1-in-9-million event and the reels celebrate about one spin in five. Fixed: one definition (e.g. "all three slots tier 3"), used by both the odds line and the cue. Distinct from the recorded with-replacement deviation (:77).

## Flow
- Open Affix > Roll Simulator, full pool
- Header: Godroll 0.00%
- Spin 10 times: about two spins flash the godroll win cue

## Expected impact
The odds line and the celebration describe the same event. Changing the definition changes what designers see as rare.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one godroll rule for odds and cue
Before: odds 1.1e-7 vs per-spin cue rate ~0.22 (1-(1-0.078)^3, from AFFIX_DEFS weights)
After: odds equals the empirical cue rate within sampling error
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: useAffixRollSimulator.tsx:72 Math.pow(minWeight / total, 3) * 100; :108 picks.map(p => p.tier === 3); :135 if (picks[i].tier === 3). AFFIX_DEFS: 35 entries, total weight 421, min weight 2; 9 tier-3 entries, weight 33.
impact: The odds line and the celebration describe the same event. Changing the definition changes what designers see as rare.
instrument: seeded Monte-Carlo test over spinAffixes picks: cue frequency vs godrollPct

title: Loot breadcrumb text is 10px and dims upcoming steps to 50% opacity
body:
## Summary
NarrativeBreadcrumb uses text-[10px] (below the repo legibility floor) and opacity 0.5 over text-muted for future steps.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/NarrativeBreadcrumb.tsx:12 carries the ESLint legibility warning (12px floor, WCAG 1.4.4), and the future-step style (NarrativeBreadcrumb.tsx:27-29) stacks opacity 0.5 on var(--text-muted), the sub-AA opacity hack the repo replaced with --text-subtle/MicroLabel. Fixed: TEXT_SCALE meta size and --text-subtle without opacity, measured with lib/contrast.ts.

## Flow
- Open Loot
- Breadcrumb renders at 10px; future steps at half opacity

## Expected impact
Readable workflow trail; slightly wider strip.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - breadcrumb meets the 12px floor and AA contrast
Before: 1 legibility warning; future-step contrast below 4.5:1 (simulated from opacity 0.5 on muted)
After: 0 warnings; contrast >= 4.5:1 via lib/contrast.ts
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: npx eslint src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/NarrativeBreadcrumb.tsx -> 12:47 warning Text below the 12px legibility floor; NarrativeBreadcrumb.tsx opacity: !isActive && !isPast ? 0.5 : 1
impact: Readable workflow trail; slightly wider strip.
instrument: contrast assertion with src/lib/contrast.ts on the computed future-step colour + eslint warning count

title: Imported item names are spliced unescaped into the generated C++
body:
## Summary
generateUE5LootTableCpp interpolates entry names into // comments and a TEXT("/Game/Items/...") path without escaping newlines, quotes or path-illegal characters.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/codegen.ts generateUE5LootTableCpp writes `// Item = "${e.name}"` and `TEXT("/Game/Items/${e.name.replace(/ /g, "_")}")`. Names come from user JSON (resolveItemName, codegen.ts:31). A name containing a newline ends the comment and injects a live statement into the pasted C++; an apostrophe ("Bacca's Blade", a shipped seed) produces an asset path UE rejects. Fixed: sanitise names for comments (strip CR/LF) and for asset paths (UE-legal charset).

## Flow
- Import { Entries: [{ Item: { Name: "X\nE.DropWeight = 9999.f;" } }] }
- Copy C++ re-export
- The injected line is live code

## Expected impact
Pasted codegen cannot carry imported text out of its comments. A stricter sanitiser could rename asset paths users relied on.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - imported text cannot alter generated code
Before: 1 injected live line per newline-bearing name (walked); seed "Bacca's Blade" yields an illegal asset path
After: 0 injected lines; asset paths in UE-legal charset
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/codegen.ts generateUE5LootTableCpp: lines.push(`//     Item = "${e.name}",`) and TEXT("/Game/Items/${e.name.replace(/ /g, '_')}"); data.ts kotor-baccas-blade name "Bacca's Blade"
impact: Pasted codegen cannot carry imported text out of its comments. A stricter sanitiser could rename asset paths users relied on.
instrument: test: generateUE5LootTableCpp over a newline-bearing and an apostrophe name; assert every non-comment line matches the expected statement set

title: BindingTuner subscribes to the whole tuning store and lints all 22 bindings to show one
body:
## Summary
useLootTuningStore() with no selector re-renders the tuner on every store write, and rosterFindings runs for every binding when only the selected one is shown.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/core/BindingTuner.tsx:41 calls useLootTuningStore() unselected; :48 memoises rosterFindings(state)[selectedId] on [state], so a pity-threshold change or any tune recomputes lintLootEconomy for all 22 bindings (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/bindingTuner.ts:368-377). Cheap today at n=22; worth a measured render-count before changing.

## Flow
- Drag the Pity tab slider
- BindingTuner (mounted on Core) re-renders and re-lints 22 bindings

## Expected impact
Fewer renders/lint passes; negligible at current roster size, so only worth it if measured.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - tuner renders only for its own inputs
Before: 22 lint passes per store write (static count); render count unmeasured
After: 1 lint pass for the selected binding
Method: simulation
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/core/BindingTuner.tsx:41 const state = useLootTuningStore(); :48 useMemo(() => rosterFindings(state)[selectedId], [state, selectedId])
impact: Fewer renders/lint passes; negligible at current roster size, so only worth it if measured.
instrument: React Profiler render count + timing over 50 setPityThreshold calls, before/after a selector split
